name: GA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sanford Bishop running with a large fundraising edge ($1.1M vs $217K)
District's Democratic lean (D+4 PVI) plus favorable national environment
Prediction markets price Bishop near 94% to win
No public polling or expert ratings available, adding uncertainty
model.rationale: Bishop combines incumbency, a heavily funded campaign, and a district that leans Democratic in a year with a favorable environment, while challenger Matt Day has raised little and shows no outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Bishop win, though thin data keeps uncertainty wide.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or polling showing Bishop under 55% would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Georgia's second district has reelected Democrat Sanford Bishop repeatedly, and he returns this cycle with a decisive financial advantage, having raised over $1.1 million to challenger Matt Day's roughly $217,000. The district's partisan lean favors Democrats by about four points, and the national environment adds to that edge. Prediction markets give Bishop roughly a 94 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, fundraising, and market pricing. That combination points to a comfortable Bishop victory, though the absence of direct polling means the margin estimate carries wider uncertainty than in better-covered districts.
